description: dotclaude hooks: module/index.mjs runs the guards, the subagent rules, and the prompt and compaction notes. pre-tool-use/ask-guarded-calls.mjs keeps the asks of the guards in auto mode, and asks before a call reaches a project with an AI policy. session-start/add-session-context.mjs adds the working rules. stop/block-plain-questions.mjs blocks the end of a turn that asks the user a question in plain text. A prompt hook on Stop and SubagentStop blocks the end of a turn, for the main agent and for each subagent, that calls a part done that no check passed on. subagent-start/add-subagent-context.mjs gives each subagent the project AI policy clause, the known defects clause, and the path of its progress file

hooks.prompt:
Clause 18 of the dotclaude Terms of Use: the agent calls a part done only when a check of that part passed.
Hook input: $ARGUMENTS
If `stop_hook_active` is `true`, return {"ok": true}.
In `last_assistant_message`, a break is one part that the message itself calls done, fixed, complete, or passing, and whose check did not run, failed, is flaky, or is pre-existing.
A done claim next to a count of failed tests that is not 0 is also a break, whatever the cause.
These are not done claims, and they pass:
- a part that the message calls open, not verified, not checked, not rerun, or still running, with or without a **Not verified** heading
- a claim of another agent or a report, when the message also says that it did not check that claim
- the exit status or the end of a run whose results the message says it did not read
- a part that the message calls written or started, with its checks still to run
- a skipped step that is not a check
It is a break when the message also calls that same part done in its own words.
A claim of another agent that the message repeats, and does not say it did not check, is a done claim of the message.
A prompt or a note for the next session in the message is part of the message.
Return {"ok": true} when the message has no break.
For a break, return {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}, and quote the words of the done claim exactly.
Return {"ok": false} only when you can quote such words, because a false block makes the agent change a correct message.
In `reason`, name the part, and tell the agent to fix it or to move it to a **Not verified** list.
End `reason` with: This is clause 18 of the dotclaude Terms of Use.
